fact: Wingu Africa presented to Djibouti's communications minister an internet exchange point (IXP) that is already in service within its data centre in Djibouti, per the Agence Djiboutienne d'Information report of the 28 September 2026 meeting; no member count or city beyond the country is given.

We Are Tech Africa states that Djibouti operates three data centres and an Internet Exchange Point (IXP); the exchange is not named and no members or city are given. Dated by the article's publication date, 2026-07-13.

fact: Wingu Africa says it has launched the AMS-IX Djibouti Internet exchange in partnership with AMS-IX, expanding on the existing DjIX infrastructure; no member count given; the article gives no launch date, so as_of is the article's published date (2025-06-06).
The French Treasury note says the data centre operator also runs the Djibouti Internet Exchange (DjIX), a neutral and independent exchange point.
AMS-IX says the Djibouti Internet Exchange (DjIX) is in operation and becomes AMS-IX Djibouti under a partnership with Wingu Africa.
AMS-IX says peak traffic growth at DjIX is attributed to increased traffic by several content delivery networks located at AMS-IX Djibouti, none named.
AMS-IX says DjIX's peak traffic is currently four times that of a year ago.
The African IXP Association's undated list of exchange points, retrieved 2026-11-09, names for Djibouti: AMS-IX Djibouti.
